summary.intent: Land the remaining performance and determinism fixes for the caliper semantic/docgen pipeline (heap-meter clamp, private-name handling, declared.symbol single-flight), measure the merged batch against the pre-batch baseline, and then assess which identified performance issues remain.
summary.outcome: Fixed a review finding on #512 (quoted members mistaken for private names) with a mutation-proven test and pushed it. Published PR bodies for #511 and #512. Measured the merged batch as faster on all five corpora with identical component and prop counts. A worker is still running the declared.symbol single-flight. About half the identified performance issues remain open.

repo: Checker private names arrive as escaped `__#N@#type`; SymbolInfo unescapes names before downstream code sees them, so private/symbol-key classification must use the raw escaped name at read time.
react-spectrum output after the private-name fix differs only by 767 renames from `__#N@#type` to `#type`.
Validation gates: `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `just test-checker-lane`, and `cargo nextest run --workspace`.

An Entire change belongs to exactly one trail, so the heap-meter change can't move off trail 405. Trails created: 468 cold-run cost, 469 determinism, 470 checker wire contract, 471 measurement honesty.
Adding a field to SymbolInfo breaks struct literals in test constructors (rpc.rs, component.rs, declared.rs).
Merged-batch medians vs c633fbc6: antd wall 1.70→0.45s and RSS 1,089→402MB; Chakra wall 4.29→3.08s; all five corpora were faster.

Remaining performance issues: convert memo duplicates (37% of Chakra conversions; needs a wait-cycle check to avoid deadlock), early checker session discarded on root mismatches (~7.5% CPU), 18 rayon threads and two checker programs on shadcn/Mantine, JSON boundary cost, 207k isReadonlySymbol requests on Chakra, wall-clock-dependent timeout fallback.

code.finding: Added `member_name()` on SymbolInfo, classified from the checker's escaped name; it replaces convert.rs's `property_name`, which classified the unescaped name and misread quoted members like `"__#8@#type"`.
Old `property_name` and its test were removed. Callers use `member_name()`, and tests now go through real deserialization.

workflow: Mutation-proof new tests by reintroducing the bug (classify the unescaped name) and confirming the test fails before restoring the code.
Use a separate worktree built from the pre-batch commit plus a minimal clamp as the 'before' binary, with interleaved repeated runs and median reporting under noisy load.
Don't quote stale benchmark ratios (e.g. the 15× vs RDT figure) until they are re-measured on current code.
Resolve review findings with a citation to the fixing commit and test.

friction: `gh` failed when a `cd` left the repo while publishing the #512 body, so it had to be re-run from inside the worktree.
Machine load of 17–30 during benchmarking made timing noisy, so interleaved runs were needed.
Earlier thread and program-count measurements ran under the whole-program bug, so those decisions rest on invalid data.
The heap-meter change can't be re-linked to a different trail because of the one-trail-per-change constraint.
open_items: Finish declared.symbol single-flight (trail 468); a worker is in flight and its PR body will be at /tmp/claude-501/pr-declared.md.
#511 and #512 await user review and merge.
Convert-memo single-flight needs its own design with a wait-cycle check.
Re-measure thread and checker program counts on the merged result.
Run the react-docgen-typescript comparison to get a current speed ratio.
Investigate early checker session discard on small root mismatches (116 vs 113 roots on Chakra).
Re-measure the JSON boundary to the checker.
Reduce isReadonlySymbol requests by deriving readonly from property flags (needs SymbolInfo changes).
Make the timeout fallback independent of the wall clock; low priority, with 0 timeouts in 128 runs.
Measure a real Storybook first and second start.
Re-run the weekly quality oracle on the merged batch.
